## Divide two expressions with powers {#division}

Simplify each expression first, then divide. Try this on paper.

$$\left(\frac{p^2}{q}\right)^2\div\left(\frac{p}{q^2}\right)^{-1}$$

<details name="division-working">
<summary>1. Simplify each expression</summary>

The first fraction becomes $p^4/q^2$. The negative power makes the second $q^2/p$. Write $\dfrac{p^4}{q^2}\div\dfrac{q^2}{p}$.

</details>

<details name="division-working">
<summary>2. Divide and check</summary>

Multiply by the reciprocal of the divisor: $\dfrac{p^4}{q^2}\times\dfrac{p}{q^2}=\dfrac{p^5}{q^4}$.

</details>

<details name="division-working">
<summary>Try a similar question</summary>

Simplify $\left(\dfrac{u}{v}\right)^2\div\left(\dfrac{u^2}{v}\right)^{-1}$.

</details>

<details name="division-working">
<summary>Check the retry</summary>

$\dfrac{u^2}{v^2}\div\dfrac{v}{u^2}=\dfrac{u^2}{v^2}\times\dfrac{u^2}{v}=\dfrac{u^4}{v^3}$.

</details>
